taskContent:
In a digital workshop view, the length of a strip between endpoint marks A and B is to be measured. The strip and both scales belong to the same scaled digital model. The reference labelled “2 cm” refers to that model. The illustration is not a photograph, and the screen width is not a physical centimetre scale.

![Digital workshop view with strip A–B, two scales with different subdivisions, and a model reference.](https://skillpilot.com/assets/goal-visualizations/mathematik/af8f64f1-b5bd-5201-9999-5224e3d06972/af8f64f1-b5bd-5201-9999-5224e3d06972.en.png)

1. Identify the quantity to be measured. Choose a suitable one of the two displayed scales and justify the choice. Calibrate its divisions using the 2-cm reference: state how many millimetres one small division represents. (3 marks)
2. Actually carry out the measurement on the image now: transfer both endpoint marks to the selected scale, independently read both positions, and record them with units. You may enlarge the entire view together and use a paper edge, a transparent ruler solely for alignment, or a conventional image annotation. Determine the strip length from your two readings and document the calculation. Do not use the ruler to claim a physical screen dimension. A description of what one could do does not replace the two actual readings. (4 marks)
3. Record a sensibly rounded measurement with a unit and realistic precision. Justify it using the scale divisions and the clarity of the endpoint marks; describe a concrete possible source of deviation and a suitable way to reduce it. Briefly explain why enlarging everything together makes reading easier but does not produce arbitrarily precise measurements. (3 marks)

Submit the quantity, scale choice, calibration, both endpoint readings, their difference, and the precision explanation. No personal images or data are required. If the fine scale remains unreadable after enlarging the whole view, the attempt must not be graded as a completed measurement; the same PNG must first be supplied legibly. There is no additional passing tier: the ordinary pass threshold is at least 8 of 10 marks.
solutionContent:
The required quantity is length. Scale II is suitable because it has finer divisions. The 2-cm reference spans 20 small intervals on that scale, so one interval represents 0.1 cm = 1 mm. Scale I only has 1-cm divisions and permits only a coarser estimate at these endpoint marks.

Transfer both endpoint marks to Scale II. The readings are approximately 1.2 cm on the left and 9.5 cm on the right. The strip does not start at zero, so its length is 9.5 cm − 1.2 cm = 8.3 cm = 83 mm. An equivalent, clearly documented reading in millimetres is acceptable.

8.3 cm, to approximately 1 mm, is an appropriate report. A conservative uncertainty of roughly ±1 to ±2 mm is also defensible when both endpoint readings and the display are considered explicitly. The divisions do not justify arbitrarily many decimal places. For example, a slightly tilted transfer line or blurred endpoint marks may change a reading; enlarging the whole image and carefully aligning the transfer reduce this effect. Enlargement preserves the ratio between the model strip and the scale and creates neither physical screen calibration nor new original information. This task demonstrates digital measurement and reading on a calibrated model; it does not observe placement of a measuring tool against a physical object.
